podcasts.title: The Sound and Music of Project Hail Mary
podcasts.transcript:
In Project Hail Mary, sound becomes more than atmosphere—it’s the bridge between two beings from different worlds.

Supervising Sound Editors and Sound Designers Erik Aadahl and Ethan Van der Ryn reveal how they gave Rocky a musical alien language, built the tactile world of life aboard a spacecraft, and used silence to draw us into Ryland Grace’s perspective. Their inventive work makes the vastness of space feel intimate, strange, and, at times, unnervingly quiet.

With James Ortiz’s expressive performance as Rocky and Daniel Pemberton’s score woven into the soundscape, the film’s sonic design deepens its story of communication, friendship, and empathy. This conversation offers a closer look at the craft behind one of the film’s most distinctive performances—and the sounds that make an unlikely connection feel real.

podcasts.transcript: In the new film, Tenzing, the sound design takes center stage. Major story points are expressed through the evolving sound of mountain winds and the increasing prominence of breathing as the characters ascend Mount Everest.
